src: Commission on Government Efficiency, the 2026 New York City Charter Revision Commission. Appendix A, Proposed Questions, adopted at the final public meeting on July 23, 2026.

q.t: Speed Up Process for Granting a Revocable Consent to Use Public Space
q.s: Simplify process to use public space for uses such as ramps, planters and cafes, by removing mandatory hearings and Council disapproval of sidewalk cafes, while maintaining community and Council input.
q.y: speeds up process to use public space while maintaining community input.
q.no: maintains longer process with mandatory public hearing to use public space and Council review of sidewalk cafes.

q.t: Reduce City Contractor Paperwork; Require Regular Meetings of Procurement Policy Board
q.s: Reduce paperwork for City contractors by authorizing Procurement Policy Board to simplify contractor questionnaire. Require quarterly meetings of the Procurement Policy Board. Remove mandatory hearing for required client services report.
q.y: amends Procurement Policy Board authority, including to simplify contractor questionnaire; authorizes Mayor to delegate certain contract approvals.
q.no: leaves laws unchanged, with Mayor and Comptroller maintaining longer questionnaire.

q.t: Speed Up Street Safety Projects, Disposition of Unused City Property, Office Leasing
q.s: Simplify review of street safety projects to reduce construction timelines. Fast track disposition of unused City property with approval from City Planning Commission. Expedite leasing offices used for City workforce.
q.y: simplifies street project approval, City property disposition and office leasing.
q.no: maintains intra-agency consultation for road projects, Council approval for City property dispositions and Council disapproval of office leases.

q.t: Simplify Building Permitting and Move Waterfront Permitting to Department of Buildings
q.s: Create centralized construction permits hub to simplify permitting. Move waterfront permitting from Department of Small Business Services to Department of Buildings. Allow construction approval by additional Department of Buildings officials.
q.y: simplifies permitting by authorizing a centralized permitting hub, moving waterfront permitting to Department of Buildings, and allowing additional Department of Buildings officials to issue approvals.

q.t: Set Contribution Targets for Rainy Day Fund to Promote Sufficient Budgetary Reserves
q.s: Set target amount of money to hold in reserve funds, including rainy day fund, to address unexpected financial hardships in future years, and require development of methodology to calculate contributions.
q.y: requires Mayor to develop methodology for calculating deposits to rainy day fund, with deposits subject to approval in the City budget.
q.no: leaves laws unchanged, with no reserves target.
